title: A pesar de: despite a difficulty

sections.content: You know *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32: they admit a difficulty and then say what happened anyway. This is a good pattern for rebellion and resistance, where people acted despite great risk. *A pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + a full clause.

items.spanish: A pesar de las prohibiciones, los palenques sobrevivieron durante años.
items.english: Despite the bans, the palenques survived for years.

items.spanish: A pesar de que era muy peligroso, algunas personas esclavizadas huían de las haciendas.
items.english: Although it was very dangerous, some enslaved people ran away from the haciendas.

items.spanish: Pese a la derrota, el recuerdo de Túpac Amaru siguió vivo.
items.english: Despite the defeat, the memory of Túpac Amaru lived on.

items.spanish: A pesar de ser libres, muchos artesanos tenían menos derechos.
items.english: Despite being free, many craftsmen had fewer rights.

sections.content: *A pesar de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive (*a pesar de ser libres*). Before a full clause use *a pesar de que* with the indicative when the fact is real (*a pesar de que era peligroso*).
